thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: continuous-batcher queue growth detected in us-west-2 (cluster: prod-uw2). Autoscaler triggered, node flaps observed, paging rates > baseline. Affected service: runtime-continuous-batcher. Symptoms: sudden token-latency spike, GPU memory pressure, repeated CUDA OOMs. Logs attached.
maya: ack. I'm on it — paging + node flaps, will gather logs and start triage. tagging @ashwin for runtime kernel memory leak suspicion.
ashwin: reading logs now. I'm seeing repeated `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` followed by container restart loops on batcher-uw2-05. Also kernel page-in spikes around the same time. Could be a prefetched KV cache growth + batching race.
samir: customer-sre ping — support queue has 7 customers reporting slow responses (90th latency 6-12s). One enterprise account (acct: ZetaHealth) filed an escalation about 503s during peak. Need quick mitigation and status update for support.
leo: quick telemetry: batch size distribution shifted right after the 03:12 deploy (canary). 95th token length increased but not enough to explain memory jump; looks like accumulator never empties for some request patterns — batch growth. Repro rate ~2-3/sec on a single node.
maya: logs (excerpt):
```
2026-03-14T03:14:22Z runtime-continuous-batcher[pid=1123]: alloc batch_accumulator size=384MB -> 1.2GB
2026-03-14T03:14:23Z runtime: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: failed to allocate 256000000 bytes
2026-03-14T03:14:23Z kubelet: killing container runtime-continuous-batcher (OOMKilled)
2026-03-14T03:14:24Z kernel: major_page_fault: pid=1123 comm=batch_accu  anon=512MB file=0MB
```
ashwin: mitigation proposal (short-term):
- disable KVCACHE_PREFETCH on the affected pool (env: `KVCACHE_PREFETCH=0`)
- enforce `MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=8192` and `MAX_CONCURRENT_BATCHES=4` to cap growth
- roll a targeted restart of batcher pods on nodes showing OOMs

maya: +1 to all. I'll apply the env patch to the dedicated pool for prod-uw2 and kick a rolling restart for the batcher deployment. Doing the kube commands now.
leo: while maya patches, I'm going to cordon & drain batcher-uw2-05 to stop noisy node from flapping other nodes. If necessary we'll evict pods to redistribute load.
maya: commands I'm running:
```
kubectl -n prod patch deployment/runtime-continuous-batcher -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"kv-prefetch":"off-temp"}}}}}'
kubectl -n prod set env deployment/runtime-continuous-batcher KVCACHE_PREFETCH=0 MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=8192 MAX_CONCURRENT_BATCHES=4
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/runtime-continuous-batcher
```
ops-bot: Started rollout of deployment/runtime-continuous-batcher (strategy: RollingUpdate). 2/10 pods updated.
leo: cordon/drain in progress:
```
kubectl -n prod cordon node/batcher-uw2-05
kubectl -n prod drain node/batcher-uw2-05 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
ashwin: note: if the underlying issue is a memory leak in the batch accumulation logic we might see OOMs again after restart. Rolling restart clears the GPU memory and gives breathing room.
maya: rollout status: 6/10 pods ready after restart. Observed inbound latency dip on the affected node groups. Paging rates dropped 60% in the past 4 minutes.
customer-sre: sent interim status to ZetaHealth: "We're investigating a runtime-side memory growth issue affecting a subset of requests in us-west-2. We've applied temporary safeguards and are restoring normal service; monitoring ongoing. ETA next update in 30m." They requested whether this was caused by the canary deploy.
samir: can we confirm canary relation? leo mentioned canary at 03:12.
leo: correlating — yes, canary at 03:12 touched a batching optimizer change (accumulator window logic). Canary logs show higher accumulator retention on a particular request path (requests with many streaming tool-calls). Hypothesis: optimizer combined with prefetch creates unbounded KV growth for certain sessions.
ashwin: plan (2-phase):
- Phase A (mitigation): keep KVCACHE_PREFETCH=0, cap batching tokens/concurrency, cordon noisy nodes to stop flapping, rolling restarts done.
- Phase B (root cause): revert batching optimizer patch from canary, reproduce in staging with long streaming sequences, add tighter accumulator GC and guardrails.
maya: Phase A results so far: 95th latency moved from 8.2s -> 1.4s on avg for impacted customers. No new OOM restarts in last 8 minutes on previously failing nodes. Paging still slightly elevated but trending down.
ops-bot: batcher-uw2-05 drained and cordoned. Pods rescheduled to batcher-uw2-02/03.
samir: thanks, please add a short note in the incident timeline for the support team. Also escalate to product about reverting the optimizer if Phase B reproduces.
leo: I'm creating a short reproduce harness and linking it here. Repro notes: send long streaming toolbed requests with repeated function calls and large KV keys; batcher accumulator doesn't GC until end-of-session due to missing decrement in window-merge. Patching now in a feature branch `fix/accum-gc-2026-03-14`.
maya: handoff: I'm rotating off in 30m. Summary for next on-call (@ashwin): mitigations applied (KVCACHE_PREFETCH=0, MAX_BATCH_TOKENS & MAX_CONCURRENT_BATCHES set), node batcher-uw2-05 drained, rolling restart completed, customer notifications sent. Monitoring for 2 hours and follow up on root-cause PR. Current status: degraded -> recovering. Please keep incident channel updated if you see regressions.
ashwin: taking over. I'll kick off an accelerated canary revert for the batching optimizer to staging and run the reproduce harness. If staging repros, schedule an emergency revert to production (target low-traffic minutes). Setting reminder to follow up in 1h.
ops-bot: action executed: restart pods completed. Nodes showing healthy memory usage. Alerts muted for 10 minutes to avoid noise during mitigation window.
customer-sre: updated ZetaHealth with mitigation summary and ETA for root cause: 4-6 hours. They requested postmortem and whether any data was lost (none reported so far).
maya: small log sample after mitigations:
```
2026-03-14T03:28:12Z runtime-continuous-batcher[pid=2245]: batch_accumulator size=128MB -> 256MB
2026-03-14T03:28:15Z runtime: allocate ok
2026-03-14T03:28:16Z kernel: minor_page_faults normal
```
ashwin: note to self: open a ticket to add a hard guard that forces accumulator eviction after X seconds or Y bytes, whichever first. Also add observability: per-session accumulator size metric + alert when > 512MB.
ops-bot: incident-bot annotated thread with `mitigation_applied=true`
samir: thanks team. Will prepare an initial incident summary for the on-call rotation notes and escalate the PR to the runtime owner. Leaving channel open for 2 hours for monitoring; if no regressions, close and switch to postmortem creation.
incident-bot: Incident state: recovery in progress. Silence window ends at 3523457642. Please continue monitoring.
ashwin: acknowledged. I'll update this thread with staging results and next steps for the revert + patch."
